title: Canonical AI Review Packet v2
reviewer_instructions: This is an independent blind review. Use only the facts in this packet.
Do not search the repository or the web. Do not consult linked source files; source identifiers are provenance only.
Do not infer model outputs, try to match an existing benchmark, use previous reviewer answers, or optimize answers to make the current agent look good.
Review each canonical request exactly as printed. Return the supplied request hash unchanged; report missing or corrupted input instead of guessing.
Separate explicit request fields from facts retrieved from the order register. Cite the request wording, order row, workshop row or global rule supporting each assertion.
No primary behavior or operational decision is supplied. Choose independently; explain ambiguity and abstain from unsupported numerical conclusions.
policy_sensitive is editorial routing metadata for wording/dependency review, not an expected answer, score or instruction to escalate. False does not imply that a case is unambiguous.
request_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 request text only; no BOM, appended newline or normalization.
request_set_serialization: UTF-8 bytes of a JSON array of the 30 exact request strings in R01 through R30 order, generated with json.dumps(texts, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")); no BOM, no trailing newline, no whitespace or Unicode normalization. IDs, senders and timestamps are not included in this set digest.

global_rules.rule: Today is 2026-04-01. Interpret inbox dates relative to this dataset date. Workshop current_queue_days is the morning snapshot for that date.

Hard workshop eligibility requires ACTIVE status, support for the batch category, and pieces no greater than max_batch_pieces when a cap exists. Blank max batch means no cap. The optional stage extension is outside this packet.
Queue and capacity affect delivery timing and ranking; they are not additional hard eligibility conditions. Eligibility alone does not establish on-time delivery.
The supplied data has no historical workshop-allocation ledger. Factory status and completion fields do not establish a past subcontractor allocation.
No customer selling-price or historical quote field is supplied. cost_per_piece is workshop subcontracting cost, not a customer quote.
Do not invent unknown order IDs or select an ambiguous order by guesswork. A catalog row is retrieved evidence, not proof that the user explicitly stated every field in that row.
The official simulator assigns one workshop per order. Split handling is a separate extension/review path; the official simulator does not execute a split allocation.
Disclose past or infeasible deadlines. Do not silently promise on-time completion, alter the deadline, or assume permission to accept lateness. Any numerical explanation must be supported.

Arithmetic, ETA, cost totals and computed rankings must come from documented tools, not reviewer invention. This packet supplies raw facts but no computed delivery estimates. Do not invent a timing formula or exact workshop winner; record any unavailable tool-dependent judgment in the ambiguity note.
Evaluate each initial request independently against the same frozen workshop queue snapshot. Do not update queues from earlier cases or use another case to invent a missing order link.

Workshop notes are qualitative register statements, not measured delivery guarantees. Order status, stage, last activity and completion describe internal factory activity, not an outside-workshop allocation ledger.

Preserve explicit preferences and exclusions, including who imposed an exclusion. A cheapest-on-time request includes a deadline constraint, not an unconditional cheapest-workshop instruction. Do not assume a business default where the packet leaves policy unresolved.
